ruleName: Ball hits an outside influence or the player
group: Ball hits an outside influence or the player
imagePrompt: A teen girl golfer on the fairway, with a golf trolley deliberately placed in the path of her next shot as she prepares to play, holding an iron club, with trees behind under an overcast sky.
imageAlt: Teen girl golfer places a golf trolley as a ball stopper on the fairway.

issues: Golf trolley could be positioned even more obviously in the direct path of the shot to reinforce 'deliberately placed' intent.
Slightly more overcast sky could help reinforce the weather condition, but this is minor.
imageVerification.repairPrompt: Position the golf trolley more directly in front of the golfer, clearly in the path of her next shot to emphasize the deliberate action. Make the sky appear a little more overcast to match the specified weather.

questions.title: Stopping Your Ball On Purpose With Your Things
questions.question: When do you get a penalty for using your things to stop your ball while playing?

choices.text: Your ball hits your bag by accident
You put your golf trolley in the way to stop your ball on purpose
Your ball hits another ball on the course
You put a headcover down to stop your ball from rolling away
Your ball hits a tree by accident

questions.explanation: You get a penalty if you use anything, like a trolley or headcover, on purpose to stop your ball. If your ball hits your bag, another ball, or a tree by accident, there is no penalty.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: Extra shots added to your score when you break a rule.
Things you use in golf, like your bag, clubs, trolleys, and headcovers.

questions.teachingTip: Remind kids they should never try to stop their ball with objects or equipment on purpose, but accidents are okay.
likelyMisconceptions: Kids might think hitting their own bag or equipment by accident is always a penalty.
Kids might think they can use objects to help stop their ball without a penalty.

questions.title: Deliberately stopping your ball with equipment
questions.question: In which situations would you receive a penalty for equipment stopping your ball during play?

choices.text: Your ball accidentally hits your own bag
You deliberately place a golf trolley to stop your ball
Your ball strikes another ball on the course
You purposely put a headcover to prevent your ball rolling away
The ball accidentally hits a tree

questions.explanation: There is a penalty if you use equipment or objects on purpose to stop your ball. Accidents, like hitting your bag, another ball, or a tree, have no penalty.
